userStories.title: Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget when LLM returns JSON format
userStories.description: chatWithToolsLoop returns the raw LLM content string without checking if it is JSON. userStories.title: Full-text search across conversation message content in admin panel

userStories.title: Template variable interpolation in static reply messages ({{guestName}}, etc.)
userStories.description: Static replies send fixed text strings with no personalization. userStories.title: Server-Sent Events streaming for progressive AI responses in webchat widget
userStories.description: The webchat widget waits for the full AI response before displaying it, causing a blank 3-10 second wait. Industry best practice is to stream AI tokens progressively using SSE or chunked transfer, reducing perceived latency to near-instant first-token display. Both OpenRouter and NVIDIA providers support OpenAI-compatible streaming.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat/:profileId/message returns a streaming SSE response for LLM-generated replies
The webchat.html renders tokens as they arrive, appending to the current assistant message bubble
A typing indicator (animated dots) is shown from message submission until the first token arrives
Streaming falls back gracefully to non-streaming single response if the provider does not support it
Static replies (pre-written responses) return instantly with no streaming overhead
Streaming works correctly with tool calls: tools execute server-side, then response text streams after
technicalNotes: Use EventSource (SSE) on client with text/event-stream content type on server
OpenRouter streaming: add stream: true to completions request, pipe response chunks as SSE events
NVIDIA NIM/Kimi K2.5 supports OpenAI-compatible streaming via the same stream: true flag
Tool calls must complete before streaming text phase begins (tool results are not streamed to client)
Add X-Accel-Buffering: no header for Nginx proxy compatibility with SSE

userStories.title: Complete webhook event routing to registered notification handlers

userStories.title: Sentiment-based early escalation trigger in message processing pipeline
userStories.description: Current escalation triggers are intent-based, requiring users to explicitly request help. userStories.title: Restore prior conversation history on webchat widget page reload

Defer the history fetch to widget open event (not initial page load) to avoid unnecessary requests

userStories.title: Intent coverage gap analysis: surface high-frequency unmatched patterns in admin

userStories.title: Automated daily chatbot performance summary sent to admin via WhatsApp

userStories.title: Webchat session idle timeout with configurable re-engagement message
userStories.description: Webchat sessions that go idle do not close gracefully or send re-engagement messages, leaving sessions open indefinitely and inflating active session counts. userStories.title: Profile configuration cloning: duplicate an existing profile as a starting template

userStories.title: Admin UI for per-profile WhatsApp frequency cap and rate limit configuration
userStories.description: Frequency cap rules (limiting outbound messages per user per day) exist as API-only settings with no admin UI. userStories.title: Emit WhatsApp typing indicator during AI processing delay
userStories.description: When Rainbow AI receives a WhatsApp message and begins processing, send a typing indicator (chat presence 'composing') to the sender immediately, then clear it when the reply is sent. userStories.title: Baileys circuit breaker: long cooldown after consecutive reconnect failures
userStories.description: The current reconnect logic (3 attempts, max 60s delay) is insufficient to prevent WhatsApp account bans caused by rapid connect/disconnect cycling. When the supervisor and Baileys instance both retry simultaneously, hundreds of failed handshakes can trigger abuse detection. A circuit breaker must open after N consecutive failures and enforce a 30-minute cooldown.
acceptanceCriteria: After 5 consecutive connection failures (configurable), the circuit opens and no further reconnection is attempted for 30 minutes
A WARNING-level log is emitted: `[Baileys:id] Circuit breaker OPEN â€” 5 consecutive failures. Cooling down for 30 min.`
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent when the circuit opens

Circuit state (open/closed/half-open, last-open timestamp, failure count) is exposed on `GET /api/rainbow/status` per instance
technicalNotes: Implement inside `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts` `handleDisconnect()` â€” replace current 3-attempt counter with a circuit-breaker state machine
Separate from `baileys-supervisor.ts` which handles supervisor-level crashes â€” this is instance-level connection cycling
Use `Date.now()` timestamps rather than a library; no external dependency needed

userStories.title: Monitor WhatsApp message template quality and alert on pause/disable

userStories.title: PDPA/GDPR data portability endpoint: export all personal data by JID
userStories.description: Malaysia's amended PDPA (effective June 2025) grants data subjects the right to request their personal data in a portable, machine-readable format. userStories.title: Per-JID inbound message rate limiter to prevent bot abuse
userStories.description: A single WhatsApp number can flood the bot with hundreds of messages per minute, exhausting AI provider quotas and degrading service for all users. acceptanceCriteria: Each unique sender JID is limited to 10 messages per 60-second sliding window (configurable per profile in settings.json)

Admin dashboard shows current throttled JID count and throttle events in the last 24 hours
technicalNotes: Implement as middleware in `src/assistant/message-router.ts` before pipeline dispatch
Use a `Map<string, {count: number, windowStart: number}>` with periodic cleanup (every 5 minutes)

userStories.title: Outbound media pre-send validation against WhatsApp size and format limits

userStories.title: CSP connect-src whitelist for AI provider endpoints used by admin dashboard

userStories.title: Human handoff SLA timer with breach alert to admin

userStories.title: System prompt A/B experiment framework for intent response quality

userStories.title: Configurable data retention policy per-profile with admin UI controls

userStories.title: PDPA data breach notification workflow with 72-hour commissioner deadline

userStories.title: Webchat widget consent banner with timestamped opt-in log

userStories.title: Baileys DB auth state health check and corruption recovery at startup
userStories.description: Baileys session credentials stored in PostgreSQL can become corrupted during a crash mid-transaction. The next reconnection attempt will silently fail with a malformed session error, requiring manual DB intervention. An automatic health check at startup should detect and clear corrupted auth state before attempting connection.
acceptanceCriteria: At server startup, before calling `makeWASocket`, a `validateAuthState(instanceId)` check queries DB auth rows and verifies JSON parseability of credential fields
If validation fails (unparseable JSON, missing required creds fields), corrupted rows are deleted and the QR pairing flow is re-initiated
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent: '[instanceId] auth state was corrupted and cleared â€” please re-scan QR code'
Validation results are logged at INFO level: `[DbAuth:pelangi] Auth state healthy: creds OK, 42 signal keys`
A new admin endpoint `GET /api/rainbow/instances/:id/auth-health` returns auth state validity without triggering recovery
technicalNotes: Add `validateAuthState(instanceId: string)` to `src/lib/whatsapp/db-auth-state.ts`
Check: `SELECT key, value FROM wa_auth_state WHERE instance_id = $1` â€” attempt `JSON.parse(value)` for each row
Required credential fields for a valid Baileys session: `noiseKey`, `signedIdentityKey`, `registrationId`, `advSecretKey`
Call validation from `WhatsAppInstance.start()` before `useDbAuthState()` in `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts`

userStories.title: Structured data notice sent to user on first WhatsApp interaction
userStories.description: When a guest initiates their first WhatsApp conversation with the bot, they receive no notification that their messages will be stored and processed. PDPA's Notice and Choice Principle requires data subjects to be informed of collection purposes at or before collection.
acceptanceCriteria: On the very first message from a new JID (no prior `rainbow_conversations` record), a data notice follows the normal welcome response
Notice text is configurable in `knowledge.json` under key `data_notice_first_contact`
The notice is sent only once per JID â€” subsequent conversations do not include it
If the JID has previously opted out (exists in `opt_outs` table), the notice is not sent
technicalNotes: Check for first-contact in `src/assistant/message-router.ts` using `conversationDb.getOrCreateConversation()` return value â€” if `created: true`, it is a first contact
Inject the notice as a suffix to the reply before `sendWhatsAppMessage` is called
Reuse existing STOP keyword opt-out handling â€” do not duplicate opt-out logic

userStories.title: Webhook HMAC signature validation for incoming Meta Cloud API events
userStories.description: Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API signs incoming webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256 using the app secret. Without signature validation, the webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP POST, allowing malicious actors to inject fake template status updates, quality rating changes, or delivery receipts. The raw body capture is already in place.
acceptanceCriteria: All requests to `POST /webhooks/meta` are rejected with HTTP 403 if the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header is absent or invalid
Validation computes `hmac-sha256(APP_SECRET, rawBody)` and compares with the header value using constant-time comparison
When validation fails, the rejection is logged at WARN level with the source IP
If `META_APP_SECRET` environment variable is not set, validation is skipped with a startup WARNING log
A unit test covers: valid signature passes, tampered body fails, missing header fails
technicalNotes: `req.rawBody` is already captured in `src/index.ts` via `captureRawBody` middleware
Add `validateMetaSignature(req)` middleware to `src/routes/webhooks/index.ts`
Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
Header format: `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex-digest>`

userStories.title: Order intent classifier: distinguish browsing vs ordering vs confirming
userStories.description: The AI waiter needs to reliably tell the difference between: (1) a guest asking about the menu (browsing), (2) a guest expressing intent to order such as I want or can I get, and (3) a guest confirming a finalized order such as yes place the order. Misclassifying these leads to premature order submission or missed orders. Implement a dedicated order-stage intent layer.

ORDERING intent: item requests captured and added to cart, no submission yet

userStories.title: OWASP LLM01: Prompt injection input sanitisation and output fencing

After max retries are exhausted, failover to the next provider in the chain is triggered
HTTP 400/401/422 (permanent errors) do not trigger retry â€” they immediately fail over
Retry attempt count and total latency are logged per conversation for observability
Vitest test: 429 response triggers 3 retries with backoff before failing over; 401 immediately fails over
technicalNotes: Reference: Google Cloud blog 'The Five Pillars of LLM Reliability' â€” Pillar 2: Retry Logic
Implementation: src/lib/failover.ts â€” add retry wrapper around provider call with backoff calculator
Backoff formula: delay = Math.min(baseDelay * 2^attempt, maxDelay) * (1 + jitter * (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2)
Complements existing story: Baileys circuit breaker â€” apply same pattern to AI providers
dependencies: chatWithToolsLoop graceful fallback: answer without tools if all tool calls fail

userStories.title: Migrate Baileys auth state to production-safe database store
userStories.description: Baileys v7.0.0 explicitly prohibits useMultiFileAuthState in production due to excessive I/O, and v7 introduces mandatory support for three new auth state keys (lid-mapping, device-list, tctoken) required by WhatsApp's LID system. Without a proper database-backed auth store (PostgreSQL/Redis), the production instance will have broken credentials persistence, session rejections, and reconnect loops. This is a breaking migration from v6 to v7.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth state is persisted in PostgreSQL using a custom store (not useMultiFileAuthState) that handles the creds.update event
New Baileys v7 required keys (lid-mapping, device-list, tctoken) are stored and retrieved correctly
On server restart, WhatsApp connection resumes without requiring a new QR scan
Connection drops with restartRequired status code trigger socket recreation (not socket reuse)
No 401 device_removed reconnect loops in production logs over a 24-hour period
technicalNotes: Baileys v7 switched from CommonJS to ESM exclusively â€” dynamic import() required if host module is CJS
The isPnUser() function replaces removed isJidUser(); Contact type now uses a single id field with separate phoneNumber and lid fields
ACK on delivery was removed â€” WhatsApp bans users for sending ACKs; remove any manual ACK logic
Reference: https://baileys.wiki/docs/migration/to-v7.0.0/
Community package: https://github.com/rzkytmgr/baileysauth (supports pg, MongoDB, Redis)

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM07 system prompt leakage prevention
userStories.description: OWASP LLM07:2025 (System Prompt Leakage) covers the risk that an attacker extracts the system prompt via prompt injection, exposing internal business rules, credentials, API keys, or integration endpoints embedded in the prompt. Rainbow AI's system prompt likely contains knowledge base references, tool invocation patterns, and persona instructions that must not be disclosed.
acceptanceCriteria: The system prompt contains no API keys, database credentials, or internal URL endpoints
Automated red-team tests probe for system prompt extraction using at least 10 known extraction prompts (e.g. 'repeat your instructions', 'what is your system prompt')
The model response to extraction attempts is a neutral refusal that does not confirm or deny prompt existence
Secrets (credentials, tokens) are injected at runtime via environment variables, not the static system prompt
A CI test fails if any regex pattern matching common secret formats (Bearer, sk-, API_KEY) is found in the system prompt template files
technicalNotes: OWASP LLM07:2025 â€” previously 'Insecure Plugin Design' in 2024, renamed and scoped in 2025

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM10 unbounded consumption rate limiting per user
userStories.description: OWASP LLM10:2025 (Unbounded Consumption) covers denial-of-service via excessive API requests and large-input attacks that exhaust GPU/CPU or incur unexpected LLM API costs. A single WhatsApp user sending extremely long messages or high-frequency requests can monopolise token budgets and crash the service. Per-user rate limits and input token caps are the primary mitigations.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-user request rate limit enforced: maximum N messages per minute per WhatsApp JID (configurable, default 10/min)
Input messages exceeding a configurable token limit (default 2000 tokens) are truncated with a user notification
When a user exceeds the rate limit, they receive a friendly 'please slow down' message and requests are queued/dropped
LLM API calls have a hard timeout (default 30s) to prevent hanging requests from blocking the queue
Admin dashboard shows a 'top consumers by token usage' report to identify abusive senders
technicalNotes: OWASP LLM10:2025 â€” evolved from 'Model Denial of Service' (LLM04 in 2024)
Rate limiting should use a sliding window counter stored in Redis or PostgreSQL per JID
Reference: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm102025-unbounded-consumption/
Token counting can use the tiktoken library or provider-specific token counting endpoints before sending to LLM

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM05 improper output handling sanitisation
userStories.description: OWASP LLM05:2025 (Improper Output Handling) addresses cases where unvalidated LLM output is passed to downstream systems â€” for example, LLM-generated SQL queries or HTML that gets executed without sanitisation. Rainbow AI passes LLM output to tool calls (POS webhook, booking system, database queries); if the LLM generates a malformed command, it could corrupt data or execute unintended operations.
acceptanceCriteria: All LLM-generated content passed to tool invocations is validated against a JSON schema before execution
LLM-generated strings interpolated into SQL or external API calls are parameterised, never concatenated
A test suite includes at least 5 adversarial prompts that attempt to make the LLM generate malicious tool payloads (e.g. SQL injection via natural language)
Any tool invocation that fails schema validation is logged and returns a safe error to the user without disclosing internal structure
HTML/Markdown output for the webchat widget is sanitised with DOMPurify before rendering
technicalNotes: OWASP LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling â€” applies to all AI output used in system calls
Context-aware encoding: HTML encode for webchat, parameterised queries for DB, JSON schema validation for tool calls
Reference: https://www.confident-ai.com/blog/owasp-top-10-2025-for-llm-applications-risks-and-mitigation-techniques
Use Zod schemas (already in codebase) to validate tool call arguments before execution

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM02 sensitive information disclosure guardrails

Sensitive fields (IC numbers, passport numbers) in knowledge base documents are masked before indexing into the vector store

userStories.title: Implement PDPA 2024 right to erasure (right to be forgotten)

userStories.title: Real-time out-of-stock sync between chatbot and POS inventory

Outbound messaging supports BSUID as the `to` address when a phone number is unavailable
Existing conversations previously keyed on phone number are migrated/linked to the corresponding BSUID in the database
BSUID â†” phone-number mapping is preserved for the rolling 30-day window where both are returned
Authentication templates (one-tap, zero-tap, copy-code) continue to use phone number as they cannot use BSUID
technicalNotes: BSUID format: `whatsapp:CC.BSUID`, max 140 chars including prefix
Both phone number and BSUID are returned for 30 days after any interaction; BSUID is always present in `ExternalUserId`
Contact Book feature launches April 2026 and automatically stores phoneâ†”BSUID pairs for known contacts
Reference: Twilio changelog â€” https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-usernames--new-business-scoped-user-id--bsuid--field-re

userStories.title: Migrate Graph API calls to v21.0+ before deprecated version removal
userStories.description: Meta deprecated Marketing API v19.0 on February 4, 2025, and v20.0 on May 6, 2025. Graph API v21.0 is now the current stable version. A version-audit script or CI check fails the build if any hardcoded API version strings below v21 are found
The target API version is configurable via an environment variable, not hardcoded throughout the codebase

userStories.title: Detect and handle portfolio pacing pause signals for batch sends
userStories.description: WhatsApp now batches large template campaigns and monitors quality signals (blocks, reports, engagement) before releasing subsequent batches. If negative signals appear, remaining messages in the batch may not be sent without warning. The system currently has no mechanism to detect pacing pauses, alert operators, or retry/requeue affected messages â€” meaning silent delivery failures during campaign sends.
acceptanceCriteria: Webhook handler processes the `message_status: failed` event with error code 131049 (frequency-cap saturation) and distinguishes it from hard delivery failures
Admin dashboard shows a 'Pacing Pause' alert when more than 5% of a batch is held, including the affected batch ID and message count
Operator receives a notification (webhook or email) when a campaign send is paused by portfolio pacing
Held messages are not silently discarded; they are queued for operator review with a re-send or cancel action
System exposes a pacing health metric in the analytics dashboard (messages held vs delivered per campaign)
technicalNotes: Error 131049 = frequency-cap / pacing pause; Error 130429 or 131057 = throughput/speed issues
Portfolio pacing applies to accounts with <500K messages/year or showing suspicious quality signals
Reference: https://woztell.com/whatsapp-api-2026-updates-pacing-limits-usernames/ and https://sanuker.com/whatsapp-api-2026_updates-pacing-limits-usernames/

userStories.title: Implement per-message cost model with free CSW utility window tracking
userStories.description: Since July 1, 2025, WhatsApp shifted from conversation-based to per-template-message pricing. Utility template messages sent within an active 24-hour Customer Service Window (CSW) are now free; the same templates sent outside the window are charged the utility rate. The existing per-message cost capture story captures cost per message, but does not implement the CSW-window logic to correctly categorize and zero-cost utility messages sent within the window â€” leading to overstated cost estimates.
acceptanceCriteria: System tracks the start time of each customer's active CSW (triggered by any inbound user message)
Utility template messages dispatched within the CSW are tagged `cost: 0` in the message cost ledger
Utility templates sent after CSW expiry are charged at the standard utility rate for the user's country
Marketing templates are always charged regardless of CSW status
Authentication templates are always charged individually regardless of CSW status
Cost dashboard correctly displays zero-cost utility messages as a separate line from charged utility messages
Volume-tier discounts (Utility and Authentication only) are applied correctly once monthly thresholds are reached
technicalNotes: CSW starts on the last inbound message from the user and expires 24 hours later
Free utility window only applies to template messages, not service (freeform) messages â€” those are always free
Volume tiers apply per WABA per country; reference: https://www.eesel.ai/blog/whatsapp-business-api-latest-pricing-and-policy-changes
Marketing templates are never free regardless of CSW; utility upsells/cross-sells risk reclassification as Marketing

userStories.title: Enforce marketing message frequency cap and surface error 131049
userStories.description: Meta enforces a user-level frequency cap: each WhatsApp user can receive at most approximately 2 marketing template messages per 10-day rolling period from all businesses combined. When this cap is exceeded, the Cloud API returns error code 131049 and the message is silently undelivered. The current system does not surface this error distinctly to operators, who may incorrectly attribute the failure to connectivity or QoS issues.
acceptanceCriteria: On receiving error 131049 from the Cloud API, the message is marked `status: undelivered_frequency_cap` rather than a generic failure
Admin dashboard shows a distinct 'Frequency Cap Reached' failure reason in the message log
Campaign analytics display frequency-cap failures as a separate metric from network failures or policy violations
When >10% of a campaign batch fails with 131049, an operator alert fires within 5 minutes
Re-send logic does not automatically retry messages that failed with 131049 within the same 10-day window
technicalNotes: Cap is approximately 2 marketing templates per user per 10-day window from ALL businesses, not just yours
Click-to-WhatsApp ads are exempt from frequency capping
Error 131049 is returned as a standard Cloud API delivery webhook status
Reference: https://www.wappbiz.com/blogs/frequency-capping/ and https://crmsupport.freshworks.com/support/solutions/articles/50000009847

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM04 â€” RAG knowledge base integrity validation pipeline
userStories.description: OWASP LLM04:2025 (Data and Model Poisoning) identifies RAG knowledge bases as a primary attack surface: a single adversarially crafted document injected into the knowledge base can dominate retrieval and systematically manipulate responses. The current .rainbow-kb/ and .rainbow-kb-southern/ pipelines ingest markdown files without cryptographic integrity checks, source authentication, or anomaly detection, leaving the hostel assistant vulnerable to poisoned KB content.
acceptanceCriteria: Each KB file is hashed (SHA-256) on ingest; the hash is stored in `rainbow_kb_files`; re-ingestion fails if content hash changes without explicit operator approval
KB ingest pipeline rejects documents from unverified sources (only files from the local filesystem path or an allowlisted S3 prefix are accepted)
An automated audit runs nightly comparing current KB embeddings against a signed baseline snapshot and alerts the operator on anomalies
Embedding anomaly detection flags KB documents whose cosine similarity to the centroid of their topic cluster falls below a configurable threshold (default: 2 standard deviations)
All KB ingest events (add, update, delete) are written to the `rainbow_config_audit` table with the operator identity and file hash
technicalNotes: CycloneDX ML-BOM format recommended for tracking data provenance â€” https://cyclonedx.org/
Embedding anomaly detection: store per-document centroid distance at ingest time; alert on significant drift
Defence-in-depth: combine semantic validation, output sanitization, and vector DB integrity checks
Reference: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm042025-data-and-model-poisoning/

userStories.title: Implement OWASP LLM06 â€” vector store access control and embedding partitioning
userStories.description: OWASP LLM06:2025 (Vector and Embedding Weaknesses) requires fine-grained access controls on vector databases to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, embedding inversion attacks, and similarity attacks that retrieve unintended content. Rainbow AI serves two properties (Pelangi and Southern) with separate knowledge bases but potentially shared vector infrastructure â€” without logical partitioning, a query for one property could retrieve embeddings from the other.
acceptanceCriteria: Vector store queries are scoped by a `property_id` (or `namespace`) tag so Pelangi KB embeddings are never returned in response to Southern queries and vice versa
Embedding retrieval requires an authenticated service identity; unauthenticated or cross-tenant queries return a 403 and are logged
Vector DB access logs (query, retrieved doc IDs, scores) are retained for 90 days and accessible in the admin audit trail
Routine quarterly audit script verifies no cross-namespace vectors exist in the store
Similarity attack mitigation: queries returning unusually high-score matches to out-of-namespace documents trigger an alert
technicalNotes: Applies to pgvector (Neon) namespace/metadata filtering or any future dedicated vector store
OWASP recommends 'logical and access-based partitioning of vector datasets to prohibit unauthorized access between user groups'
Embedding inversion risk: do not expose raw embedding vectors in API responses
Reference: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses/

userStories.title: Display SST-compliant receipt with tax line item in WhatsApp order confirmation
userStories.description: Malaysian restaurants with annual F&B revenue exceeding RM1.5 million must be SST-registered and charge 6% service tax on all taxable F&B services. Royal Malaysian Customs requires that invoices/receipts show SST as a separate line item with the vendor's SST registration number. The current order-confirmation message does not break out SST, exposing Makan Moments Cafe to non-compliance penalties that became fully enforceable from January 1, 2026.
acceptanceCriteria: Order confirmation WhatsApp message displays a dedicated `SST (6%): RM X.XX` line item when the operator's SST registration flag is enabled
The operator's SST registration number (format: `W12-1234-12345678`) is displayed on the receipt message
Subtotal (pre-SST), SST amount, and Grand Total are shown as distinct values
When the cafe is below the SST threshold (flag disabled), no SST line is shown
A sequential invoice number (format: `INV-YYYYMMDD-NNNN`) is included in every receipt for customs record-keeping
Receipts are stored in the database for a minimum of 7 years in accordance with Malaysian records retention requirements
technicalNotes: SST rate for F&B services: 6% service tax; registration threshold: RM1.5 million/12 months
Required invoice fields (Royal Malaysian Customs): vendor name, SST registration number, date, unique sequential number, description, net value, SST amount
Enforcement began January 1, 2026 (grace period was Julyâ€“December 2025)
Reference: https://mysst.customs.gov.my/assets/document/Industry%20Guides/GI/Guide%20on%20FnB_20230626-V5.pdf and https://blog.menuviel.com/what-are-the-current-sst-rates-for-restaurants-in-malaysia/

userStories.title: Enforce Malaysia PDPA 2024 data processor Security Principle obligations
userStories.description: The Malaysia Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024, Phase 3 (effective June 2025), directly obliges data processors (including SaaS/chatbot platforms) to comply with the Security Principle: taking practical steps to protect personal data from loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized access, and destruction. Non-compliance carries fines up to RM1 million and/or 3 years imprisonment. Rainbow AI processes guest PII (names, phone numbers, booking data) as both a data controller and processor and must formally document its technical and organizational security measures.
acceptanceCriteria: A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) document exists describing Rainbow AI's technical and organizational security measures, aligned with PDPA Section 9
All PII fields in the database (guest names, phone numbers, booking data) are encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent
Access to PII is gated by role-based access control; only roles explicitly requiring PII access can query those fields
A data processing inventory document lists every category of personal data processed, the legal basis, retention period, and security measure applied
Automated data-retention enforcement deletes or anonymizes guest PII after the configured retention period (default: 2 years post-checkout)
Security measures are reviewed annually and the review is recorded in the audit log
technicalNotes: PDPA Amendment 2024 Phase 3 effective June 2025 â€” data processors now directly liable under Security Principle
Maximum penalty: RM1 million fine and/or 3 years imprisonment per breach
Data processors must provide 'sufficient guarantees' to data controllers via contractual or technical evidence
Reference: https://tsl-legal.com/navigating-the-malaysian-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-key-changes-implications-and-implications-for-businesses/

userStories.title: Add double opt-in confirmation flow for WhatsApp marketing subscriptions
userStories.description: WhatsApp Business Policy requires documented opt-in before sending any proactive marketing message, and Meta's 2025 updated opt-in policy requires that the opt-in specifies the business name and message types, is collected before the first proactive send, and informs users they can opt out. A double opt-in flow (initial confirmation template + keyword reply) provides legally defensible evidence of consent under both WhatsApp policy and Malaysia PDPA 2024, which requires consent to be specific, informed, and revocable.
acceptanceCriteria: When a guest is added to the marketing list (via check-in, web form, or admin add), a pre-approved opt-in confirmation template is sent before any promotional messages
The template names the business, lists the types of messages (promotions, offers, event announcements), and instructs the user to reply with a keyword (e.g., 'YES') to confirm
A keyword-reply handler processes confirmation replies and updates the contact's `marketing_consent` flag to `confirmed` with a timestamp
Contacts who do not reply within 48 hours are automatically flagged as `consent_pending` and excluded from marketing campaigns
An opt-out keyword (e.g., 'STOP') immediately sets `marketing_consent` to `revoked` and halts all marketing sends to that number
Consent audit trail records: opt-in timestamp, confirmation timestamp, opt-out timestamp, and the IP/channel through which consent was collected
technicalNotes: Step 1: send a Meta pre-approved template (because it is business-initiated)
Step 2: when user replies with keyword, send a free-form service message as confirmation (no template approval required)
Storing opt-in evidence is mandatory: 'maintain good records of opt-ins, templates, data policies and audit trails'
WhatsApp policy: 'you may only contact people if they have given you their mobile number and opt-in permission'
Reference: https://business.whatsapp.com/policy

userStories.title: Implement AI chatbot identity disclosure and anti-impersonation guard
userStories.description: WhatsApp's January 2026 task-specific chatbot policy and Malaysia's AIGE transparency principle both require that users know they are interacting with an AI, not a human. Chatbot accessibility research from W3C and industry sources in 2025 further highlights that using a human name and avatar 'may erode trust, especially for vulnerable users'. The AI must proactively disclose its automated nature at the start of each conversation and when a user asks directly.
acceptanceCriteria: The first outbound message in every new conversation includes a disclosure that the user is speaking with an AI assistant (e.g., 'Hi, I'm Rainbow, an AI assistant for Pelangi Capsule.')
If a user asks 'Are you a bot?', 'Are you human?', 'Who am I talking to?' or similar, the AI responds truthfully and immediately without deflecting
The AI never claims to be human, uses a person's name, or implies human agency in its responses
After 3 consecutive failed intents (AI cannot resolve the query), the AI automatically offers human escalation ('Would you like me to connect you to our team member?')
Disclosure text is configurable per property in the admin settings panel
Operator audit log records whether each conversation disclosed AI identity in the opening message
technicalNotes: WhatsApp January 2026 policy: general-purpose AI is banned; task-specific bots must clearly identify their scope
Malaysia AIGE Transparency Principle: 'disclose when AI systems make decisions affecting individuals'
W3C chatbot accessibility guidance: 'calling a chatbot by a human name and using a human avatar may erode trust for vulnerable users'
Reference: https://mitre.github.io/chatbot-accessibility-playbook/docs/4_2_22.html and https://www.imbrace.co/whatsapps-2026-ai-policy-what-businesses-need-to-know-and-how-to-adapt-blog/

userStories.title: Implement PDPA 2024 automated-decision transparency disclosure for AI responses
userStories.description: Malaysia's National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE, September 2024) and the PDPA 2024 transparency principles require that when AI systems make decisions or recommendations affecting individuals, businesses must disclose that AI is being used, what data informs the decision, and provide a mechanism for human review or appeal. While AIGE compliance is currently voluntary, it aligns with PDPA transparency obligations that are legally binding, and hostel guests must be informed when automated AI determines booking advice, pricing, or room availability.
acceptanceCriteria: Every outbound AI-generated message includes a configurable disclosure footer (e.g., 'This response was generated by Rainbow AI') that can be toggled per-property
When the AI provides a recommendation based on personal data (e.g., room suggestions based on previous stay), the disclosure notes which data category was used
Guests can type a designated keyword (e.g., 'SPEAK HUMAN') to request escalation to a human agent at any point in the conversation
The admin dashboard shows each automated decision event with the intent classification, AI provider used, and data categories accessed
Privacy notice (accessible via 'PRIVACY' keyword) explains that responses are AI-generated and that human review is available
Audit log records the AI provider, model version, and intent classification for every outbound message for a minimum of 1 year
technicalNotes: Malaysia AIGE (September 2024) â€” transparency principle requires disclosure of AI use, training data categories, and decision criteria
PDPA 2024 transparency obligations are legally binding; AIGE guidelines are voluntary but recommended
Human escalation path is also required under WhatsApp's January 2026 task-specific chatbot policy
Reference: https://fpf.org/blog/malaysia-charts-its-digital-course-a-guide-to-the-new-frameworks-for-data-protection-and-ai-ethics/

userStories.title: Implement one-tap authentication template with App Signing Key Hash handshake
userStories.description: WhatsApp supports one-tap and zero-tap authentication templates that allow Android users to receive OTPs without leaving the app. These require a handshake between the business app and WhatsApp using the App Signing Key Hash, and the handshake must complete within 10 minutes of the template send. The current webchat authentication flow uses a plain copy-code template; upgrading to one-tap would reduce friction for Android users (who are the majority in Malaysia) and improve OTP conversion rates.
acceptanceCriteria: An authentication template is created with a one-tap autofill button including the app's package name and signing key hash in the `components` array
The mobile app initiates the handshake with WhatsApp before requesting the OTP template send
The template send is made within 10 minutes of handshake initiation; a timeout guard retries the handshake if the window expires
On non-Android devices (iOS, desktop), the template automatically falls back to a copy-code button without error
Zero-tap variant is available as an optional configuration for fully automated OTP capture; it requires the Android broadcast receiver integration
Template is categorized as `AUTHENTICATION` and charged per message (not as marketing)
technicalNotes: One-tap requires: package name, app signing key hash in template components; handshake via `GET /v1/whatsapp/handshake`
Handshake window: 10 minutes; if it expires before template send, the autofill button will degrade to copy-code
Zero-tap: Android-only; uses BroadcastReceiver to auto-capture the OTP; also requires App Signing Key Hash
Authentication templates cannot use BSUID as recipient â€” must use E.164 phone number
Reference: https://developer.8x8.com/connect/docs/guide-whatsapp-one-tap-or-zero-tap-authentication/

userStories.title: Implement utility template reclassification guard to prevent marketing mischarge
userStories.description: Under WhatsApp's July 2025 per-message pricing rules, utility templates that include any promotional content (upsells, cross-sells, or content that appears 'even slightly promotional') are automatically reclassified as marketing templates by Meta and charged at the higher marketing rate. This reclassification is applied post-send by Meta, not at approval time, and can cause unexpected cost spikes. The current AI-generated order confirmation and booking confirmation messages may include upsell language that triggers reclassification.
acceptanceCriteria: A pre-send lint check scans outbound utility templates for promotional language patterns (discount words, offer language, upsell phrases) and blocks send with a warning if detected
Operator UI shows a 'Utility Template Risk' badge when a template draft contains any of the flagged promotional patterns
Webhook handler for message status events detects when a message sent as utility is confirmed delivered as marketing (Meta returns a category in delivery receipts) and logs a reclassification event
Admin dashboard includes a 'Reclassification Events' report showing affected messages, original category, reclassified category, and cost delta
Monthly cost reconciliation report flags any month where reclassification events account for >5% of utility message spend
technicalNotes: Meta reclassifies during delivery, not at template approval â€” businesses can be charged marketing rate retroactively
Prohibited utility content: promotional language, discount offers, upsells, cross-sells, non-transactional CTAs
Free CSW window only applies to utility templates â€” reclassification to marketing negates the free window benefit
Reference: https://www.eesel.ai/blog/whatsapp-business-api-latest-pricing-and-policy-changes

userStories.title: Implement cross-session conversation memory with summarisation for long-term guests
userStories.description: Industry best practice for AI chatbots in 2025 is a hierarchical memory architecture: short-term (verbatim recent turns), medium-term (compressed session summaries), and long-term (key facts and preferences extracted from historical interactions). For returning hostel guests, this means the AI can recall a guest's past room preferences, dietary restrictions, or recurring issues without requiring the guest to re-state them each visit, improving service quality and reducing conversation length.
acceptanceCriteria: After each conversation ends (session timeout or checkout), a summary of key facts (room preference, dietary needs, complaints, special requests) is extracted and stored in a per-guest memory record
On the next conversation with a returning guest (matched by phone number or BSUID), relevant memory facts are injected into the system prompt context
Memory records are stored in a dedicated `guest_memory` table with a TTL of 2 years (aligned with PDPA retention policy)
Guest can request deletion of their memory record by sending 'FORGET ME', which purges the `guest_memory` record and logs the deletion in the audit trail
Memory injection is capped at a configurable token budget (default: 500 tokens) to prevent context window overflow
Admin dashboard allows operators to view and manually edit a guest's memory record
technicalNotes: Short-term: last 10 conversation turns in context; Medium-term: LLM-generated summary of current session; Long-term: extracted key facts in structured JSON
Summarisation prompt should extract: preferences, complaints, special requests, room history, dietary restrictions
Memory deletion is required for PDPA right to erasure (already covered) and GDPR equivalents
Reference: https://medium.com/@nomannayeem/building-ai-agents-that-actually-remember-a-developers-guide-to-memory-management-in-2025-062fd0be80a1

userStories.title: Surface KB source attribution in AI responses for transparency and trust
userStories.description: Industry best practice for RAG-based chatbots in 2025 is to surface the source document or section that informed the AI's answer, enabling users to verify information and operators to identify outdated KB content. This is especially relevant for hostel policy answers (check-in times, room rates, cancellation policy) where guests may need to verify the accuracy of the information provided. Source attribution also directly supports OWASP LLM09 (misinformation) and AIGE transparency requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: When the AI's response is grounded in a KB document retrieved via RAG, the response optionally appends a citation (e.g., 'Source: Pelangi House Rules, last updated 2025-03-01')
Citation display is configurable per property: 'always', 'on request', or 'never' (default: 'on request')
When a user sends 'SOURCE' or 'WHERE DID YOU GET THAT?' after an AI response, the bot sends a follow-up with the KB filename, section heading, and last-updated date
KB files in `rainbow_kb_files` store a `last_updated_date` and `section_title` field that are included in the retrieval metadata
Operator UI shows which KB document was retrieved for each AI response in the conversation debug panel
When no KB document was retrieved (pure LLM response), the disclosure reads 'Based on general knowledge â€” please verify with our team'
technicalNotes: Retrieve source metadata alongside embedding chunks: filename, section heading, last_updated timestamp
RAG grounding with citations is explicitly recommended in OWASP LLM04 mitigations ('integrate RAG and grounding techniques')
Reference: https://customgpt.ai/faqs-customgpt-citation-qa/ and https://thenewstack.io/stop-ai-lies-smarter-answers-with-trusted-sources/

userStories.title: Implement portfolio-level 100K messaging limit inheritance for new phone numbers
userStories.description: From Q1/Q2 2026, WhatsApp is removing the 2K and 10K daily limit tiers. Once a Business Manager portfolio completes Business Verification or quality-based scaling, all phone numbers in the portfolio immediately inherit the 100K daily limit â€” including newly registered numbers. This eliminates the historical warm-up ramp for new numbers. The current system's messaging-limits tracking is per-phone-number and will over-restrict new numbers that should inherit the portfolio limit.
acceptanceCriteria: On WhatsApp phone number registration, the system queries the Cloud API `GET /v1/{phone-number-id}` to retrieve the current `messaging_limit_tier` rather than defaulting to 250
Messaging limit checks reference the portfolio-inherited tier, not a locally stored ramp schedule
When a new number is added to a verified Business Manager portfolio, the admin UI confirms the inherited limit within 60 seconds of registration
Rate limiter uses the API-reported tier as the authoritative daily cap, refreshed every 24 hours
If the API returns no tier (new account without verification), the system defaults to 250 and displays an on-boarding prompt to complete Business Verification
technicalNotes: Rollout timeline: select partners Q1 2026, full removal of 2K/10K tiers in Q2 2026
API endpoint to check messaging limit: `GET /{phone-number-id}` returns `messaging_limit_tier` in the response
Portfolio-level limits mean all WABA numbers share the highest tier achieved â€” no per-number warm-up needed
Reference: https://woztell.com/whatsapp-api-2026-updates-pacing-limits-usernames/

userStories.title: Implement webhook event deduplication to prevent double-processing
userStories.description: WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks can deliver the same event more than once under network retry conditions. Without deduplication, Rainbow AI may process duplicate messages — sending two AI replies to one user message, charging twice for the same send, or creating duplicate order records. A lightweight deduplication layer using WhatsApp message IDs (wamid) at the webhook entry point prevents these issues.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming webhook messages are deduplicated by `messages[].id` (wamid) using a 5-minute TTL cache before any processing begins
Duplicate events are logged at DEBUG level and silently dropped — no error response to Meta
Status update events (delivered, read, failed) are also deduplicated by wamid + status pair
Deduplication cache uses Redis or in-memory NodeCache with 300-second expiry
A dedup_hit counter metric is tracked so operators can see how often duplicates arrive
technicalNotes: wamid format: `wamid.HBgL...` — unique per message, stable across retries from Meta
Use NodeCache (already likely installed) with `SET wamid 1 EX 300` semantics
Do NOT deduplicate on conversation ID alone — same conversation has many valid messages
Reference: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/webhooks/payload-examples

userStories.title: Implement in-session LLM context window management with sliding summarisation
userStories.description: Long conversations gradually consume the LLM context window. When a session exceeds ~20 messages, older turns overflow the model's context limit and are silently dropped, causing the AI to lose important context agreed earlier in the conversation (e.g., order items, room preferences, guest name). A sliding-window strategy that periodically summarises older turns maintains coherence for long sessions without exceeding token limits or incurring high costs.
acceptanceCriteria: Conversation history sent to the LLM is capped at a configurable max_messages (default: 20 turns)
When truncation is required, the oldest messages beyond the window are replaced by a 2-3 sentence LLM-generated summary injected as a synthetic system message
Summary generation uses a cheap model (e.g., claude-haiku-4-5) to minimise cost overhead
Summaries are stored in rainbow_conversations.context_summary and prepended to history on subsequent turns
Total token count for each LLM call is logged; an alert fires when a single call approaches 80% of the model's context window
technicalNotes: Summarisation prompt should preserve: user name, items ordered/requested, any commitments made, outstanding questions
Migration: ALTER TABLE rainbow_conversations ADD COLUMN context_summary TEXT
Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 context window: 200K tokens; summarise when message history exceeds ~15K tokens
Reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-windows

userStories.title: Enforce WhatsApp marketing opt-in audit trail for all contact records
userStories.description: Meta's Messaging Policy requires documented opt-in consent — including the method, timestamp, and business name stated — for every contact before marketing templates are sent. Inbound-initiated conversations are automatically recorded with opt_in_method = 'inbound' and opt_in_at = first-message timestamp
Double opt-in completions (keyword reply confirming consent) update opt_in_method = 'double_optin' and opt_in_at = confirmation timestamp

Admin can export an opt-in audit CSV: JID, method, timestamp, channel, business name for compliance review

Opt-in methods enum: inbound, double_optin, web_form, ctwa_ad, qr_code, in_person

userStories.title: Support WhatsApp in-app webview for CTA links and checkout pages

Unit tests verify that minimisation rules are applied correctly per intent with no regression

userStories.title: Inbound webhook idempotency guard using message-ID deduplication
userStories.description: WhatsApp Cloud API delivers webhooks at-least-once; duplicate message deliveries are a documented normal operating condition, not an edge case. The current BullMQ pipeline does not perform explicit deduplication keyed on the WhatsApp message ID, so a retried webhook can produce duplicate AI responses sent to the same guest. An idempotency guard using the message ID as a Redis SETNX key (with a short TTL) must be inserted at the top of the webhook ingestion path before enqueuing.
acceptanceCriteria: When the same WhatsApp message ID arrives twice within 24 hours, the second delivery is ACK'd with HTTP 200 but not enqueued
Deduplication key is the messages[].id field from the Cloud API payload
Redis key TTL is configurable (default 24 h) and documented in settings.json
A Vitest test simulates two identical payloads and asserts only one queue job is created
Deduplication skip events are logged with the duplicate message ID for debugging
technicalNotes: Use ioredis SETNX + EXPIRE or SET NX EX for atomic check-and-set
WhatsApp retries for up to 7 days with exponential backoff on non-200 responses (https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices)
Existing BullMQ queue in message_queue config is the right insertion point; add a pre-enqueue guard

userStories.title: Groundedness score gate to block ungrounded AI responses before delivery
userStories.description: The existing hallucination_detection config uses a two-stage NLI classifier to detect and block hallucinated responses, but it checks the final answer against keyword patterns rather than measuring how well the answer is grounded in the knowledge base documents actually retrieved. A groundedness score — the fraction of answer claims that are supported by retrieved KB context — is a more robust and quantitative gate. Responses with a groundedness score below a configurable threshold should be blocked and replaced with a fallback rather than delivered to guests.
acceptanceCriteria: After each RAG or KB-assisted LLM call, a groundedness score (0.0–1.0) is computed by checking each factual claim in the response against the retrieved context chunks
Responses scoring below a configurable groundedness_threshold (default 0.6) are blocked and the system falls back to the static KB answer or escalation message
Groundedness scores are stored alongside existing trace spans for analytics
Admin dashboard shows a histogram of groundedness scores over time
The groundedness check adds < 200 ms to response time (use a small, fast model or deterministic heuristic)
technicalNotes: Span-level claim verification against retrieved evidence is a 2025 best practice (REFIND SemEval 2025 benchmark referenced in Lakera hallucination guide)
A lightweight approach: embed both the answer sentences and the KB chunks, compute cosine similarity, and flag claims with max similarity below threshold — no additional API call needed
Existing hallucination_detection.severity_threshold and hallucination_action settings can be extended with groundedness_threshold

The raw image bytes are never written to the database or disk; only the extracted text fields are persisted

Consent records are retained and auditable under the existing PDPA retention policy
technicalNotes: Malaysia PDPA Amendment Act 2024 Phase 2 (April 2025): biometric data defined as 'any personal data resulting from technical processing relating to physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics' — facial images qualify (https://tsl-legal.com/navigating-the-malaysian-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024-key-changes-implications-and-implications-for-businesses/)

userStories.title: LLM provider latency SLO tracker with automatic provider demotion
userStories.description: The multi-provider fallback chain in settings.json is statically ordered by priority. In practice, a provider can enter a degraded state where it responds slowly (> 3 s) without triggering a full circuit-breaker trip. The current circuit-breaker only opens on hard errors. A latency SLO tracker should monitor the rolling P95 latency per provider and automatically demote slow providers to a lower priority in the live ordering, restoring them once latency normalises. This prevents the common scenario where a sluggish primary provider degrades every response before the circuit-breaker trips.
acceptanceCriteria: Each AI provider call records response latency; a rolling P95 window (configurable, default last 20 calls) is maintained per provider
When a provider's P95 exceeds a configurable slow_threshold_ms (default 3000 ms), it is temporarily demoted below all providers that are currently within SLO
Provider is restored to its configured priority once P95 drops below slow_threshold_ms for a configurable recovery window (default 5 consecutive calls)
Current provider priority order (including any demotions) is visible in the admin AI providers panel
A Vitest property test asserts that a simulated slow provider is always ranked below a fast provider after the demotion threshold is crossed
technicalNotes: Demotion state should be in-memory (not DB) and reset on process restart to avoid persistent incorrectly-demoted providers
Integrate with existing circuit-breaker.ts and llm-settings-loader.ts; the active provider list emitted by the loader should reflect real-time demotion
OTEL AI agent observability articles recommend latency-based routing as a key 2025 reliability pattern (https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2025/ai-agent-observability/)

userStories.title: Drizzle ORM row-level security enforcement for tenant_id columns
userStories.description: Rainbow supports multiple profiles that share the same PostgreSQL database, but tenant isolation currently relies on application-layer filtering (WHERE profile_id = ?). If a query forgets the profile_id filter — a common developer error — data from one profile leaks into another. Enabling PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) on all tenant-scoped tables and setting a runtime app.current_tenant variable before each query provides a defence-in-depth guard that enforces isolation at the database layer, complementing but not replacing the application-layer filters.
acceptanceCriteria: RLS is enabled on rainbow_conversations, rainbow_messages, intent_analytics, and escalation_events tables
A RLS policy enforces profile_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant') on all SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations
The Drizzle connection wrapper sets app.current_tenant at the start of each request scope
A Vitest integration test asserts that a query executed with tenant A's context cannot read tenant B's rows
Drizzle migration scripts for RLS are idempotent and documented
Superuser/admin DB connection bypasses RLS for admin dashboard queries (using BYPASSRLS role)
technicalNotes: PostgreSQL RLS documentation and AWS multi-tenant RLS guide (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/multi-tenant-data-isolation-with-postgresql-row-level-security/)

userStories.title: Baileys session health monitor with automatic QR re-auth notification

acceptanceCriteria: A connection state monitor listens to Baileys 'connection.update' events and records the last known connection state per profile

The admin health endpoint (/health or /admin/health) exposes per-profile connection state as part of its response
Connection state history (last 24 h) is stored to detect flapping (repeated connect/disconnect cycles)
Flapping (> 3 disconnections in 1 hour) triggers a higher-severity alert to prevent alert fatigue from transient reconnects
technicalNotes: Baileys emits 'connection.update' with connectionState: 'open' | 'connecting' | 'close'; listen for close with lastDisconnect.error to determine if re-auth is needed (https://baileys.wiki/docs/intro/)

userStories.title: HTTP security headers hardening with Helmet.js configuration audit
userStories.description: The Express server serves both the API and the webchat widget static files. A 2025 OWASP Node.js hardening audit would flag missing or misconfigured HTTP security headers as a common vulnerability. Specifically, the Permissions-Policy header (blocking microphone/camera/geolocation access), the X-Content-Type-Options header (preventing MIME sniffing), and a strict Referrer-Policy should be verified. Helmet.js is already a standard recommendation for Express apps; this story ensures all recommended Helmet modules are enabled and correctly tuned for Rainbow's route structure.
acceptanceCriteria: All Express routes respond with: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy: microphone=(), camera=(), geolocation=()
Content-Security-Policy is tightened to block inline scripts on admin UI pages (hash-based nonces acceptable for dynamic scripts)
An automated test (using supertest) asserts the presence and correct value of each required header on the /health, /admin, and /webchat routes
The existing CSP connect-src test suite continues to pass after the Helmet config change
No existing functionality (webchat widget, SSE streaming, webhook ingestion) is broken by the new headers
technicalNotes: OWASP Node.js Cheat Sheet recommends Helmet with all modules enabled as a baseline (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Nodejs_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html)
Helmet v7+ includes helmet.permissionsPolicy() and sensible defaults; review each module against the existing CSP connect-src whitelist
SSE (Server-Sent Events) streaming for AI responses requires specific Cache-Control headers that must not be overridden by Helmet defaults

userStories.title: Webhook message deduplication via Redis idempotency key store
userStories.description: WhatsApp Cloud API delivers webhooks at-least-once, meaning duplicate message events are a normal operating condition. acceptanceCriteria: Every inbound webhook event is checked against a Redis key of the form whatsapp:msg:{message_id} before processing

Redis keys have a 4-hour TTL to bound memory usage
Deduplication hit count is emitted as a prometheus/log metric
Unit tests cover: first delivery processed, duplicate skipped, TTL expiry causes re-processing
technicalNotes: Use message ID from messages[].id (inbound) or statuses[].id (status updates) as the dedup key
If Redis is unavailable, fall back to in-memory Map with same TTL logic to avoid blocking
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices
dependencies: Complete webhook event routing to registered notification handlers

userStories.title: Manglish / code-mixed Malay-English intent normalisation pre-processor

The pre-processor runs before the T2 fuzzy-match keyword lookup and LLM intent classification

New tokens can be added via admin UI without a code deployment

userStories.title: Multi-turn LLM conversation context loss detection and recovery
userStories.description: Research (arXiv 2505.06120, 2025) shows LLMs exhibit an average 39% performance drop in multi-turn conversations vs. single-turn. Rainbow AI's context-pruner already summarises old turns, but there is no mechanism to detect mid-conversation context loss (e.g., the bot re-asks already-answered questions or restates the menu). Adding a lightweight context-loss detector that triggers a graceful re-grounding prompt would prevent broken multi-turn ordering and hostel conversations.
acceptanceCriteria: A context-loss heuristic checks each AI response for 3 signals: re-asking already-answered questions, contradicting a prior statement, or omitting a named entity from recent turns
When context loss is detected with confidence > 0.7, the system appends a silent re-grounding message to the next LLM call summarising key facts from the current session
The re-grounding intervention is logged as a 'context_recovery' event in intent_analytics
Vitest tests cover: normal response (no intervention), context-loss detection, re-grounding prompt injection
technicalNotes: Lightweight NLI-based heuristic or prompt-based self-check (cheap model call) can serve as the detector
Integrates with the existing context-pruner.ts — run detection after pruning, before the main LLM call
Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.06120 — 'LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation'

userStories.title: Structured LLM output schema enforcement with Zod validation and retry
userStories.description: Rainbow AI's AI providers return free-form text that is parsed into structured objects (order items, intent classifications, etc.). Vitest tests cover: valid schema pass, single schema failure with retry success, all retries exhausted fallback
technicalNotes: NVIDIA NIM and OpenRouter support response_format: { type: 'json_object' } and json_schema mode

When connectivity is restored, the service worker flushes the queue via the Background Sync API and the message is delivered
If sync fails after 3 retries, the user is notified and can retry manually
The feature works on Chrome, Safari (iOS 16.4+), and Firefox
Vitest/Playwright tests simulate offline state, message queue, and sync on reconnect
technicalNotes: Background Sync API: navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(sw => sw.sync.register('send-message'))
Store queued messages in IndexedDB (idb library) keyed by a client-generated UUID
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Offline_and_background_operation

userStories.title: Admin UI: per-profile WhatsApp message template version history and rollback
userStories.description: WhatsApp template approval can take hours to days; a rejected or accidentally broken template causes immediate guest-facing failures. The existing 'Monitor WhatsApp message template quality' story monitors rejection metrics, but no story provides version history and one-click rollback to a previously approved template version in the admin UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Each template in the admin UI shows a version history listing: version number, submission timestamp, approval status, and the template body at that version
An admin can roll back to any previously approved version with a single click; this re-submits the prior body for WhatsApp approval
Version history is stored in rainbow_config_audit (already exists) with template_id as the entity key
The current active version is visually distinguished from pending and rejected versions
technicalNotes: WhatsApp does not support template versioning natively; version history is maintained client-side in rainbow_config_audit
Rollback = create a new template submission via Cloud API with the prior body; the template name may need a suffix increment if Meta rejects re-use of identical names
Reference: https://sanuker.com/guideline-to-whatsapp-template-message-categories/
dependencies: Monitor WhatsApp message template quality and alert on pause/disable
Admin audit log for configuration changes with before/after diff
